# Opening Perspectives loses the cockpit rail's clicked state

## Context

Follow-up to merged #19509, filed separately at the operator's request so #19502 remains paired with its one merged PR. Vega found the failure while validating [Institution #650](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/pull/650); Sophie independently reproduced it.

Controlled consumer: Institution `d2485dbe58e8608347fc7f3da71a573ed19a061a`, Brain `2445eb360f284c3e7208e2b02371f826a1d98c5c`, Node 24.19, Playwright 1.63. All non-Engine dependency versions were held to the same lock and themes rebuilt before each run.

| Engine | Full visual suite |
|---|---|
| `d75cc68543d2bc19d9c37760d5de1ed87cc426e8` | 51/51 |
| `7aae7c3166b7fc35ace2550763681791bb84e7f4` | 50/51; Perspectives pressed-state assertion fails |
| `a43fdd381ba10742bd62d0a35817a27fcad77b17` | 50/51; Perspectives passes, a different Home-field settling assertion fails |

Vega also reports a 51/51 `a43fdd38` control and two failing `7aae7c31` full runs; her failing artifacts were overwritten. Sophie's failing trace, error context and terminal worker-state attachment are retained. The tighter independent `a43fdd38` run passes the rail case but is not an all-green suite: its different Home-field settling failure is retained without attributing it to this producer. Source comparison `a43fdd381b..7aae7c3166 -- src` changes only `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs`; that is a regression locator, not yet the mechanism.

## Current witness (2026-10-09, Engine `1671fdc56b`)

The unchanged fixed-lock full suite passes **51/51**, but that is not closure. The earlier version comparison is timing-sensitive: a diagnostic build with all five runtime/SCSS files changed since `7aae7c31` restored byte-for-byte to that earlier version also passes 51/51 now. Reversing only #19525 passes 51/51 too. These controls do not establish a causal fix.

A focused browser witness reproduces the loss **3/3 on the current unmodified candidate**, using two consecutive real Playwright mouse clicks: Golden Path, then Perspectives. Read-only wrappers record the existing methods; renderers and worker transport remain real. No sleeps, retried clicks or forced pressed classes are involved.

| Event (App-worker performance time, ms; first arm) | Observed state |
|---|---|
| 964.5: `setActiveItem(stream-tabs, goldenPath)` projection queued | prior strip selection |
| 965.3: refresh begins | staged reconciliation active |
| 979.7: Rail 1 accepts Perspectives | `revealed-focused`; button 51 `pressed: true` |
| 1144.4: refresh completes | Rail 1 unregistered; replacement Rail 2 `idle`, `revealedItemId: null` |
| settled read | new button 127 `pressed: false`; VDOM/vnode classes and DOM all unpressed |

The other two real-mouse arms have the same identity/state loss. The slower walk passes. A test-workspace-only isolation sending selection through existing `retainTopology` preserves Rail 1 and button 51 with matching App/VDOM/vnode/DOM state in 3/3 arms. That establishes identity retention as the useful seam; it is not the chosen production fix.

## The Problem

In `test/playwright/visual/FleetCockpitVisual.spec.mjs` of the Institution, “every strip and rail pane reads one head” walks Activity → Tasks → Memories → Mailbox → Catch up → Golden Path → Perspectives. After the Perspectives click, the unchanged assertion waits ten seconds for its rail tab's `pressed` class.

The failing trace resolves successive button IDs **137 → 142 → 151** during that wait. A diagnostic that runs only after failure finds:

- the surviving Perspectives button has `pressed: false` in App state;
- its VDOM and vnode both lack `pressed`;
- `needsVdomUpdate` and `isVdomUpdating` are false;
- its rail's reveal machine is `idle`, with `revealedItemId: null`.

This is not a pressed class stranded on the same component. The earlier committed strip selection finishes its staged projection after a newer rail reveal was accepted, destroying the accepting rail and constructing an idle replacement. A full-suite pass alone does not discharge this timing failure.

## The Architectural Reality

- `dashboard/dock/interaction/Rail.mjs:onTabClick` feeds the reveal machine; `syncRevealedTabState` writes each button's `pressed` config.
- `button/Base.mjs:afterSetPressed` projects that config into its class list.
- `dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` and `projection/Reconciler.mjs:reconcileProjection` own committed projection and chrome lifetimes.
- `projection/Reconciler.mjs:prepareTabChromeProjection` and `moveRetainedTabChrome` preserve tabs nodes during a staged projection; edge rails are currently rebuilt. The stable-topology path already retains rail instances and updates their `railItems` / `dockZoneDocument`.
- `Rail.afterSetRailItems` already calls `reconcileTabs` and `syncRevealOverlay`; new reveal machinery is not needed. Source verified at `1671fdc56b`.
- `setActiveItem` currently takes the staged path. Other topology commits can replace an unchanged rail too; Ada independently witnessed an already-open reveal being reset by reconciliation.

**Design authority:** Rail's documented click contract opens a focused transient reveal, and its tab state shows which pane is revealed. The existing consumer assertion enforces that contract.

## The Fix

Retain an unchanged edge-rail instance through staged reconciliation, as existing tabs chrome is retained. Match structural rail identity, edge and membership; reparent the live rail into the staged shell and update its document/metadata through the existing reactive seam. Its reveal machine, bound overlay and pressed buttons survive by identity. Edge or membership changes retain the established rebuild/retirement behavior.

This is the agreed Ada/Sophie shape. Routing only selection through a fast path would fix the witnessed pair but leave unchanged rails vulnerable to other staged commits. Copying/replaying reveal state into a replacement would re-run entry/focus behavior. Neither is the selected repair.

No new caller argument, user obligation or wire format is proposed. Decision Record impact: none; this extends the existing retained-chrome mechanism.

## Contract Ledger

Surface lookups: current `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` staged planner/mover and stable rail update path; `Rail.afterSetRailItems` at `1671fdc56b`. New private helpers, if needed, remain implementation details.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Reconciler.reconcileProjection(options)`, staged path | Rail's click/reveal contract; this defect's accepted-intent witness | A rail with matching dock identity, edge and membership survives by instance identity, including its reveal machine, overlay binding and pressed tab. Existing options/results remain compatible. | Changed edge/membership, absent or replaced structural identity follows the existing rebuild/retirement path. Failure cleanup must not destroy a retained live rail as discarded staging chrome. | Reconciler JSDoc documents retained rail ownership beside tabs | Real unit identity/state assertions; browser accepted-click witness; failure/changed-membership controls |
| `Rail.railItems`, `Rail.dockZoneDocument` and `afterSetRailItems` | Existing reactive rail seam | Retained rails receive the new committed metadata/document through existing setters; no separate reveal-state copy or replay API | A removed reveal target follows existing rail reconciliation semantics; no revived dismissed intent or duplicate pane/overlay | Existing seam plus planner/mover ownership notes | State and DOM agree; pane/overlay/tab identity and metadata checks |



## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The request/transition is identified with App/VDOM/vnode/DOM evidence: an older staged selection projection destroys the accepting rail; see current witness above.
- [ ] Regression coverage is red before the repair and green afterward: an already-open reveal and a reveal accepted during a pending staged projection retain the same unchanged rail, pane/overlay binding and pressed tab. A changed edge/membership and projection failure remain safe.
- [ ] The full Institution visual suite passes on the repaired Engine with the same locked non-Engine inputs and rebuilt themes. Keep the original assertions and goldens; an isolated green run is insufficient.
- [ ] Any VDOM behavior change has real App → VDom → Main → App E2E coverage in dedicated and shared worker modes, plus relevant unit controls.

## Out of Scope

The independent structural-overlap repair (#19513), Dock blank frame (#19514), root nesting (#19521), and grid stale highlight (#19515) retain their own tickets and owners. Do not assume they share this producer. No installed-app replacement or live-harness restart.

## Avoided Traps

A successful Playwright click is not proof the same component survives. “Full-suite dependent” is observed; state leaked by an earlier test is not established. Installing an Engine without saving must still verify the rest of the dependency graph; a refreshed Playwright version invalidates a one-variable comparison.
